## To Discuss

- Reading the table's limits. The most common U1 error, 7 of 25: 1 kt classified as Force 0. The table says Force 0 is `< 1` and Force 1 is `1 - 3`, so the first test is `wind < 1`, not `wind <= 1`. 
- Testing both limits. 12 of 25 write each band as `wind >= 17 && wind <= 21`. Once the `elseif` chain is ordered by upper limit, reaching a branch means every earlier test was false, so the lower limit already holds. One-sided tests are shorter, leave no gaps and are not prone to copy-paste mistakes.  Each method has pros/cons - just make sure you understand them both. 
- What should a negative speed return? The specification asks only for defined behavior for any real number, so any answer passed U2. You chose -1 with "Invalid", "NaN", "Calm", an `error(...)` and more; 3 of 25 take `abs()` first, which turns -10 kts into 10 kts, Gentle Breeze. Worth a vote: which of these does the caller want?
- Fruitful functions return; they do not typically print (context dependent). 9 of 25 print inside the function. 
- Sea-state wording. Four functions return names that differ from the table: three only in capitalization ("Moderate breeze", "calm"), one with different names. The background picture at the top of `beaufort_main.m` uses sentence case and runs to Force 12; the specification table below it is the one to match. Single (char array) and double quotes (strings) both pass - we'll talk about the different data types this week!
- Use indention to make your  code readable.
